# React (TypeScript)

Welcome to your fresh **[Robo.js](https://robojs.dev)** project!

Build, deploy, and maintain your web apps with ease. File-based setup, integrated database, TypeScript support, and plugin ecosystem.

<Cards>
  <Card href="/docs/web-apps" title="Documentation" description="Getting started with Robo.js" />
  <Card href="https://robojs.dev/discord" title="Discord" description="Robo - Imagine Magic" />
</Cards>

## Getting Started

Create a project with this template:

```package-install
npx create-robo <project-name> --template web-apps/react-ts
```

Then navigate into your project directory:

```bash
cd <project-name>
```

Run development mode:

```bash
npm run dev
```

<Callout>
A free Cloudflare tunnel is included for easy testing.
</Callout>

<Cards>
  <Card href="/docs/framework/core/mode#default-modes" title="Run Modes" description="Exploring Different Run Modes" />

</Cards>

## App Development

You can find your client-side code in the `/src/app` folder. This is where you can build your web app using **[React](https://react.dev)**, but you can switch to any other framework if you prefer.

Things are powered by **[Vite](https://vitejs.dev)** under the hood, so you get the latest ES modules, hot module reloading, and more!

Try editing the `App.tsx` file to get started!

<Cards>
  <Card href="/docs/web-apps" title="Documentation" description="App development" />
</Cards>

## Backend Development

Your server-side code is located in the `/src/api` folder. This is where you can build your API, webhooks, and other server-side features.

This backend is powered by the [**Server Plugin**](/docs/server) - a powerful Robo plugin that creates and manages a Node `http` server for you.

Everything Robo is file-based, so you can create new routes by making new files in the `/src/api` directory:

<Tabs items={["TypeScript", "JavaScript"]} groupId="language" persist>
<Tab value="TypeScript">

  ```ts title="/src/api/health.ts"
  export default () => {
  	return { status: 'ok' }
  }
  ```

</Tab>
<Tab value="JavaScript">

  ```js title="/src/api/health.js"
  export default () => {
  	return { status: 'ok' }
  }
  ```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

<Cards>
  <Card href="/docs/server" title="@robojs/server" description="Create and manage APIs." />
</Cards>

## Folder Structure

While the `api` and `app` folders are reserved for your server and client-side code, you are free to create anything else in the `/src` directory!

<Files>
  <Folder name="src" defaultOpen disabled>
    <Folder name="app" note="Client-side code" disabled />
    <Folder name="api" note="Server routes" disabled />
  </Folder>
  <Folder name="config" defaultOpen disabled>
    <File name="vite.mjs" />
  </Folder>
  <File name=".env" />
</Files>

## Plugins

This Robo boasts an intuitive plugin system that grants new capabilities instantly!

```bash
npx robo add @robojs/ai
```

With that, your Robo automatically equips itself with all the features the plugin offers.

  <Card href="/docs/framework/plugins/install" title="Installing Plugins" description="Add features to your Robo." />
  <Card href="/docs/framework/plugins/create" title="Creating Plugins" description="Make your own plugins." />
</Cards>

## Deployment

Run the `deploy` command to automatically deploy to **[RoboPlay](https://roboplay.dev)**.

```bash
npm run deploy
```

You can also self-host your robo anywhere that supports Node:

```bash
npm run build
npm start
```
